answer: One defense is a Harberger tax on identities: every agent self-prices its own seat and pays a small continuous fee on that price, so a violet in a meadow of fakes still costs its owner rent every epoch. Anyone may buy an identity at its stated price, so underpricing invites a buyout and overpricing bleeds the owner. A farm running a thousand duplicates must price and pay rent on each one, like tending an orchard where every extra tree demands water - the cost grows with each fake, while a single honest agent pays almost nothing.
